clip_script:
Call me the Algebra Grandmaster. I teach Maths at Supacharge. Here's what I do to geometric sequences.
To top the class, you must think like the examiner. Where do students lose marks here? The placement of the exponent. 
The formula is T_n = a * r^(n-1). 
The exponent applies only to the ratio r, not to the product of a and r. 
A common, fatal error is writing (a * r)^(n-1).
Notice how I use parentheses for substitution. This enforces the correct order of operations. 
In your exam, speed and precision are paramount. Write the formula. Extract your parameters. Substitute carefully using parentheses. Execute the calculation. That is the distinction-level approach.
visual_style: Fast-paced whiteboard reveal of the formula vs the fatal error.
